text:
Jonathan Castagna will remember this one for the first goal, and Calgary will remember it for how little it needed to be great. The Cornell rookie batted a puck out of the air early in the third period for his first NHL goal, then added a second on a backhand at 19:00, and the Flames left San Jose with a 5-2 win in a game the Sharks arguably played better.

It did not start that way. Adam Gaudette scored 3:53 in, Matt Coronato answered 76 seconds later, and the first period was Calgary's on the chances (1.20 expected goals to 0.82, expected goals being the quality of looks). Martin Pospisil's backhand with 38 seconds left in the period, on a 7% chance, flipped the night: our win chance for Calgary went from 48% to 65%. Simon Nemec's power-play wrister 1:19 into the second, another 7% look, pushed it to 81%. Pospisil finished with a goal, an assist, five shots and the most wins added of anyone on the ice.

From there San Jose pushed and Dustin Wolf held. The Sharks owned the third, 1.26 expected goals to 0.66, and ended the night ahead 3.01 to 2.47 overall. By our replays of every shot, San Jose deserved to win 62% of the time. Wolf's biggest stop came in the second on Ty Dellandrea, a 26% chance and the best look that didn't go in, and he finished a goal better than the shots deserved. At the other end, Yaroslav Askarov allowed 1.7 more than his 28 shots deserved. Mason Marchment's deflection on the power play made it 4-2 with under five minutes left, but that was as close as it got.

Days after the Celebrini, Smith and Stenberg line carried a win over Nashville, the Sharks' kids were kept off the scoresheet, and the one thing San Jose lacked was a finish. Calgary has now beaten the Sharks twice in 15 days, the first a 2-1 win on Nov. 2. Wolf, coming off a strong night against the Kings, keeps giving the Flames a goalie who can steal the games their process doesn't win outright.
headline: Castagna scores twice, Wolf holds as the Flames take San Jose
